title: Restore a dishwasher rack that comes off its track
instruction: Press the loose wheel back onto the dishwasher rack, then roll the rack into the tub on both tracks and let go.
context: A backed-out dishwasher rack wheel can fall off when the basket crosses the door joint. Pressing it back into place restores support so the rack rolls in level.
setup: A cool and unplugged 550 × 500 × 438 mm countertop dishwasher has its 360 mm door fully open. Two 28 mm tracks run from its door into the tub. An empty wire basket (390 × 460 mm, about 0.8 kg) begins partly out on its three attached wheels. The 34 × 9 mm nylon front wheel with the spoke mark rests on its rail 3.65 mm out from its seated position, aligned with the axle but clear of the retaining lip. The README gives the layout and track marks. An oak press block with a rectangular grip rests on the counter outside the open door.
scoring: 0.25 when the roller sits within 2.5 mm of its axle datum, within 9° of its axis, and supports the basket on the track with the grippers clear for 0.5 s. Score 0.5 after at least 75 mm of supported hinge crossing, with wheel clearance no more than 3 mm and its rolled arc within 14 mm of its translation. Score 1.0 when the intact rack is also at least 5 mm inside the tub, resting on both tracks with the arms clear for 0.5 s. A damaged or tipped assembly or one that leaves the work area scores 0.
reset_notes: Restore the rack and sound wheels to their marks. Stand the loose roller on its rail at the backed-out position. Reset robot and part state, scorer history and camera buffers. Return the press block to its counter position.
fidelity: The complete cabinet, open door, original track transition and freely rolling basket remain assembled. Two compliant slider lips represent the snap hub. Wheel, clip and rail dimensions are estimates based on the reference assembly. Small wire dividers are visual and structural bars carry contact. The appliance stays unpowered. The free wooden block transmits the push through its flat face.
